Chilliness, (20. d.) Chilliness in the room,
legs in die open air, (a. 12 d.) Momentary shaking as
from chilliness, with goose-flesh. Passing shudder-
ing through the trunk, from time to time. Constant
shuddering down the trunk, without chilliness. Super-
ficial warmth of the body, with icy-cold hands. Dry heat
in the evening, after a walk of 16 miles, with thirst and
burning in the eyes. Great warmth in the whole hody,
afier going to bed. Small, quick pvlse. Jnaines to
sweat profusely, on every exertion of the body. She
sweats a good deal when sitting, especially the upper part
of the body. Copious morning-sweat. Sourish mornmg-
sweuts and subsequent hoarseness.

ZINCUM.

Take a piece of pure metallic zinc, and, holding it under
distilled water, rub some of the zinc off upon a fine setting-
stone, dry the powder which falls to the botiom, upon a
sheet of white blotting paper, and prepare one grain of it
in the manner recommended for the dry substances.

Zinc has cured affections characterised by one or more
of the following symptoms : Want of disposition to work
and to walk ; she thinks that she will die ; weak memory ;
constant obtusion of the head ; gloominess ; sore pain in
the head ; humming in the head ; pain of the hairy
scalp, as if there were sub-cutaneous ulceration ; baldness ;
dryness of the eyes; amaurosis with contraction of the
pupils ; paralysis and falling of the eye-lids ; humming in
the ears ; loose teeth ; painfullness of the teeth when chew-
ing; sore toothache ; salt taste in the mouth ; pressure at
the stomach with nausea after eating bread ; lensive pain
in the sides of the abdomen; inguinal hernia; constipa-
tion; loose and liquid stool; involuntary discharge of
fasces ; itching of the anus ; retention of urine when he
wants to urinate ; involuntary micturition while walking ;

inability to retain the urine when coughing, sneezing or
walking; continual erections in the night; loo rapid emis-
sion of the ssmen during an embrace ; too early menses ;
painful menstruation; distension of the abdomen during
the menses; leucorrhoea ; coryza ; cough; tensive pain in
the sternum ; palpitation of the heart with anxiety ; irregu-
lar, spasmodic movements of the heart; shocks of the
heart arresting the breathing ; intermission of the beats of
the heart, arresting the breathing ; pain in the small of the
back; pain in the back; drawing pain in the arm of long
standing; feeling of dryness of the hands, early in the
morning; the fingers go to sleep, in the morning when
rising; stiffness of the tarsal joint after sitting; painful
chilblains on the feet ; insensibility in the body ; feeling of
coldnej.s in the bones ; excrescences ; drowsiness in the
morning when rising ; drowsiness after a meal ; sleep full
of fancies'; frightful dreams ; talking and exclaiming while
asleep ; inclination to perspire in the day-lime ; night-
sweat.

Camphor moderates the effects of zinc for a short while;

they are sometimes moderated by smelling of Ignatia ;

Hepar. snip, is the best antidote.

My' co-observers are: Franz, Hartmann, Hanbold,

Riickert, Stapf, Gersdorff, Lesquereur, Schweikert, Rum-
el, Hartlaub, Ng.

Moral Symptoms. — Desponding and sad. Taciturn
and out of humor, especially in the evening. Exces-
sively sullen and peevish. Low-spirited. Unconquerable
sadness. Anxiety caused by thieves or horrid phantoms
which he sees when waking, as if in a state of feverish
fancy. Despondency. Thinks calmly of dying, in the
afiernoon, feeling exhausted. Hypochondriac mood, three
hours after dinner, with pressure under the last ribs, espe-
cially on the right side ; aversion to work and uncom-
fortablencss of the whole body, but without a trace of
flatulence or overloading the stomach, (a. 5 d.) Relaxa-
tion of the moral energies. Indifference, (a. 13 d ) Aver-
sion to labor. Inclines to internal rancor and chaorin ;
he is taciturn and dislikes to speak a single word.° He
moans from chagrin, without any apparent cause, with an
aching pain in the upper part of the head. Is easily carried

away by anger. He would like to have some one upon
whom he could wreak his anger, (which breaks forth
without any apparent cause.) Irritable, starts easily. The
talking of other people and every liule noise are intolerant
to him. Every little emotion causes an inward tremor.
After a little emotion he trembles for along while, as with
chilliness. His imagination is excited. Talking of others,
even of persons who are dear to him, makes him nervous
and peevish. Impatient, but without ill-humor. Change-
able mood, sad and melancholy at noon, cheerful and con-
tented in the evening, (2. 3. d.) By turns, irritable, in-
clining to start, angry, desponding, melancholy. A trifle
can excite his laughter or his anger. Lazy and out of
humor the first days, cheerful afterward. Illusion of the
fancy, when holding the head down, as if she had a tall
head, over which she cannot look. Incoherent ideas, (a.
10 d.) Absence of thought, the mind being in a sort of
stupor. Forgetful.
